author: Acemoglu, Daron and Restrepo, Pascual
title: Automation and new tasks: How technology displaces and reinstates labor
supported_claim: Automation can displace labor; new tasks can reinstate it.
interpretation_limit: Motivates separating productivity and employment; no fitted digitalization effect.
edition_note: Metadata and cited claim agree with the primary publication source.

author: Alice H. Amsden
title: Asia's Next Giant: {South Korea} and Late Industrialization
supported_claim: Late industrialization involves learning from earlier innovators.
interpretation_limit: The 1989 edition is retained. A DOI for the 1992 OUP edition is not assigned to it.
edition_note: Original 1989 edition retained; 1992 paperback DOI not transferred. OUP 1992 landing page only corroborates the argument.

author: Atkinson, Anthony B.
title: On the Measurement of Inequality
supported_claim: Equally distributed equivalent aggregation relates distribution to inequality aversion.
interpretation_limit: The model adapts a power mean to group welfare, not observed incomes or estimated individual utility.
edition_note: Activate the archived methodological reference for welfare aggregation.

author: Bankes, Steve
title: Exploratory modeling for policy analysis
supported_claim: Computational experiments support reasoning under substantial uncertainty.
interpretation_limit: Exploratory use is distinct from fitted prediction.
edition_note: Metadata and cited claim agree with the primary publication source.

supported_claim: A micro-to-macro model links consumption, production structure, growth and distribution.

edition_note: Use 2010 issue year (61(1), 180–218); early online publication was 2009. Add DOI and correct title punctuation.

title: Digital economics

author: David Harvey
title: The New Imperialism
supported_claim: Accumulation by dispossession concerns appropriation and changing control.
interpretation_limit: Chapter 4 is the content source; the book landing-page abstract was inconsistent and was not used.
edition_note: Add verified book DOI; conceptual support checked in Chapter 4 rather than erroneous landing-page abstract.

title: Premature deindustrialization
supported_claim: Manufacturing shares peak at lower incomes in later industrializers.
interpretation_limit: Supports the structural-change problem, not the specific conjectured negative correlation.

supported_claim: Data accumulation and extraction can be examined as political-economic processes.
interpretation_limit: Does not make simulated investment reallocation proof of dispossession.
edition_note: Publisher PDF first page confirms 1–12 despite an empty Crossref page field. Registered article number: 2053951718820549.
